questions.q: Approximately how much does an Oracle Fusion Cloud practice instance cost, and for how long?
options: It is billed per setup task completed
About $85 for three months of access
About $850 for one year of access
It is a one-time lifetime purchase
questions.explain: As last verified, OracleERPGuide's practice instance runs approximately $85 for roughly three months of access — verify current pricing before purchasing.

options: A single setup task
The named container FSM uses to hold a generated, trackable task list for a rollout
A type of chart of accounts value set
A legal entity's registered address
questions.explain: An implementation project is created by selecting offerings and functional areas, and FSM builds the hierarchical task list inside it.

questions.q: In order from largest to smallest, how does Oracle Fusion organize setup work?
options: Setup task, then functional area, then offering
Offering, then functional area, then setup task
Functional area, then offering, then setup task
There is no consistent organization
questions.explain: The hierarchy runs offering (e.g. Financials) down to functional area (e.g. Enterprise Profile) down to the individual setup task.

questions.q: Why is over-engineering enterprise structures (extra ledgers or charts of accounts 'just in case') a problem?
options: Oracle Fusion technically limits you to one structure anyway
It has no cost since storage is unlimited
It is not a problem; more structures are always safer
Every extra structure must be configured, maintained, and reconciled indefinitely
questions.explain: Each additional structure adds ongoing configuration, maintenance, and reconciliation burden, which is why simpler designs are generally preferred.

questions.q: Why does Oracle Fusion offer a guided Accounting Configuration Manager flow instead of only isolated setup tasks?
options: Because building a primary ledger with its legal entities and business units together is such a common combination that a connected flow reduces the chance of a missed link
Because legal entities cannot exist without this tool
Because the chart of accounts is created inside this tool only
Because isolated tasks are technically impossible to complete
questions.explain: The guided flow exists because this combination of pieces is configured together so often, and configuring them in isolation makes it easy to forget a required connection.

questions.q: What are the four defining characteristics (the "4 C's") of every Oracle Fusion ledger?
options: Chart of accounts, calendar, currency, and accounting method
Cost center, customer, credit, and collections
Code, class, category, and class type
Company, country, currency, calendar
questions.explain: Every ledger is defined by its chart of accounts, calendar, currency, and subledger accounting method.

questions.q: What mechanism, previewed in this lesson and expanded later, controls which company policies (like payment terms or approval limits) apply to a transaction based on its business unit?
options: Cross-validation rules
Reference data sets, assigned to business units
Ledger sets
Legal reporting units
questions.explain: Reference data sets, covered fully in Lesson 12, are assigned to business units and control which policies and rules apply to a given transaction.

questions.q: Why does business function assignment matter beyond being descriptive metadata?
options: It has no real effect on the system
It directly determines which setup tasks and reference data options appear for that business unit
It only affects the color of the business unit's icon
It is only relevant to legal entity registration
questions.explain: A business unit without a given function assigned will not show that function's setup tasks or reference data options at all — assigning the function unlocks that configuration surface.

options: The specific, formal address tied to a legal entity's registration
A hierarchical structure of countries and states
A shipping address for a warehouse
Any address used anywhere in Oracle Fusion
questions.explain: A legal address is the formal address a legal entity is registered against, managed through Manage Legal Address.

questions.q: Why is managing period status described as a day-to-day control rather than a one-time setup step?
options: Because period status never changes once set
Because a controller must actively open and close periods every accounting cycle as business activity and reconciliations proceed
Because period status is set automatically by the chart of accounts
Because only secondary ledgers require ongoing period management
questions.explain: Unlike one-time structural setup, period status requires ongoing attention each accounting cycle to open the next period and close the completed one appropriately.

questions.q: Why can some reports include adjusting period activity while others exclude it?
options: Adjusting periods can never appear in any report
Only secondary ledgers can have adjusting periods
Oracle Fusion does not support this flexibility at all
Because different reports answer different questions — pre-audit, regular-period numbers versus full, audited final numbers
questions.explain: Reports and balance inquiries can include or exclude adjusting period activity depending on whether pre-audit or fully audited numbers are needed.

questions.q: Which of the four predefined conversion rate types requires the preparer to manually enter a rate, with no automatic value supplied?
options: Corporate
User
Fixed
Spot
questions.explain: The User rate type is the one exception to automated rates — a rate must be typed in manually during journal entry.

questions.q: In a tree, which values do transactions actually post to?
options: Parent (summary) values only
Detail (child) values with posting allowed, not the summary parent nodes
Every value in the tree equally
Only values from a different value set entirely
questions.explain: Transactions post to detail/child values; parent (summary) nodes exist for rollup reporting rather than direct posting.

questions.q: Why does a summary/parent value typically have 'Posting Allowed' turned off?
options: Because posting allowed only applies to independent value sets
Because summary values cannot be part of any hierarchy
Because summary values are always disabled
Because transactions should post to detail values, which then roll up into the summary for reporting
questions.explain: Posting Allowed is turned off for summary/parent values since direct transactions belong on detail values, with summaries existing purely for rollup reporting.

questions.q: How does a chart of accounts structure instance differ from the structure itself?
options: A structure instance can only exist for secondary ledgers
There is no difference; the terms are interchangeable
A structure instance is an actual, usable deployment of the structure, tied to specific value sets for each segment
A structure instance defines segment order while the structure defines nothing
questions.explain: The structure instance applies specific value sets to the structure's shape, and more than one instance can share the same underlying structure.

questions.q: For what kind of company is rapid implementation generally the most appropriate approach?
options: Only companies using exclusively secondary ledgers
A complex multinational with many legal entities and extensive segment hierarchies
A company with relatively simple, single-chart-of-accounts, limited-entity requirements
Only companies with no legal entities at all
questions.explain: Rapid implementation suits simpler requirements; more complex multinational setups usually need the detailed, screen-by-screen configuration this course covered.

questions.q: What is a key flexfield, in plain terms?
options: Oracle's underlying mechanism for building a structure out of independently-defined segments that combine into one composite key
A type of legal reporting unit
A reference data determinant
A conversion rate type used for currency translation
questions.explain: A key flexfield is the technical mechanism chart of accounts structures (via the Accounting Flexfield) are built on.

questions.q: In the LTV Manufacturing Corporation worked example, which segment carries the mandatory primary balancing label?
options: Company
Account
Future
Cost Center
questions.explain: The Company segment carries the primary balancing label, with one value per legal entity (1000 for the US parent, 2000 for the Canadian subsidiary).
